subject.title: fix(mattermost): backfill thread history from server when in-memory window is empty

question: After the 200-post clamp is fixed, should a cold Mattermost thread turn await one bounded server fetch and suppress all retries for the rest of that stored session when the fetch fails?
rationale: This is an intentional session-state and availability tradeoff: retrying can repeatedly delay inbound turns, while never retrying can leave a recovered session context-free after one transient server failure.

options.title: Accept bounded once-per-session recovery
options.body: Keep the current five-second bounded fetch and no-retry marker after adding the 200-post clamp and its regression test.

options.title: Retry transient failures
options.body: Record success separately from failure and permit a tightly bounded retry policy so transient Mattermost outages do not suppress recovery for the entire session.

options.title: Pause this recovery path
options.body: Do not merge the server backfill until the channel owner chooses a different latency and failure policy.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded once-per-session recovery
recommendation.body: Keep the current five-second bounded fetch and no-retry marker after adding the 200-post clamp and its regression test.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and helped prepare the adjacent Mattermost thread/session routing implementation, so they are the strongest evidence-backed owner for this channel behavior tradeoff.
